title: Hotpatch for GPU memory spike triggered by KV-sync race under high-concurrency hosted workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers observed sudden GPU OOM spikes in the hosted API between 2025-11-10 and 2025-11-12 during high-concurrency traffic bursts. Investigation shows a KV-sync race that duplicated large KV cache segments across sessions, triggering a transient 2x memory residency and subsequent OOM cascade on heavily utilized nodes. This ticket tracks the hotpatch, rollout, verification, and customer communications for mitigation and permanent remediation.
steps_to_reproduce: Run hosted inference load harness with 1200 concurrent short-chat sessions (seq_len distribution skewed to 1024 tokens)
Enable KV-prefetch and session-pin features in route config to mimic production routing behavior
Introduce synthetic latency on backend shard that causes a slow KV sync reply (use test shim)
Observe per-GPU resident memory via metrics (nvml) and runtime logs showing duplicate KV allocations and delayed frees
mitigation_performed: Applied immediate autoscaling policy increase for affected clusters to avoid customer errors
Deployed a conservative per-session KV allocation cap in hosted config to prevent duplication explosion
Rolled back a canary autoscaler tweak that increased concurrency-per-GPU by 20%
Notified top-impacted customers and enabled routing to alternate regions for critical traffic
proposed_fix_summary: Patch runtime to synchronize KV-index updates with a light-weight epoch guard and add an atomic transfer path that prevents ephemeral duplicate KV buffers. Also add a GC fence to delay free until all execution lanes confirm release. Includes unit tests and an integration stress test that reproduces the race under throttled RPC timing.
rollout_plan: Prepare branch runtime/hotfix/ENG-53112 with tests and changelog
Run integration stress suite in staging for 24h with high-concurrency profile
Canary deploy to 5% of hosted capacity in low-traffic region for 4 hours
Monitor GPU resident memory, KV allocation counts, and error rates; if green, 25% rollout for 2 hours, then 100%
Holdback plan: automatic rollback to previous runtime if OOM rate > 0.2% during canary
verification_criteria: No GPU OOMs observed in canary for 8h under synthetic peak load
KV allocation peak is reduced to <=1.05x of baseline during bursts
Integration stress tests pass with deterministic run for 3 consecutive runs
Customer-reported errors reduced to zero for the three impacted enterprise tenants
follow_up_tasks: Backfill additional telemetry: per-session KV lifetime and transfer events
Create runbook entry for KV-sync-related OOM triage
Schedule postmortem with customers and CS to review incident and SLA impact
Root-cause doc for infra and research teams to evaluate kernel-level improvements
